Root cause. The parser calls `parseOption(optionType, offset)` and may construct an IPv6 option before any source statement proves that the bytes at the selected `offset` cover a full `someipsdhdroptionsipv6` object.
For IPv6 option types, `parseOption()` constructs `SomeIpSdIPv6Option(this, offset)` using only the data container and offset; it still receives no available-byte bound.
The constructed IPv6 option records a logical option length of `sizeof(someipsdhdroptionsipv6)`, so its accessors treat the backing pointer as a complete IPv6 option structure.

Project-code propagation. The IPv6 option keeps the `SomeIpSdLayer` as `m_DataContainer` and the selected `offset` as `m_Offset`, so `getDataPtr()` resolves to the same packet backing pointer `m_Data + offset`.

Sink. `getIpAddress()` casts that same option data pointer to `someipsdhdroptionsipv6*` and passes `hdr->ipv6Address` to `IPv6Address`; the constructor then copies 16 bytes, which the saved ASan trace reports as the overflowing read.
